title: Best Oscillating Multi-Tools UK
short: Four oscillating multi-tools compared on power, attachments and value, from a £33 budget pick to a £142 professional DeWalt.
intro: An oscillating multi-tool vibrates an attachment back and forth rapidly, turning into a sander, saw, scraper or grout remover depending on what's clicked on, and its surgical cutting action lets you cut flush against a wall or deck where a full-size saw can't reach. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup, comparing corded and cordless models on power, oscillation angle, attachments included and ease of changing blades. Prices are as reviewed.

products.name: PMF 220 CE
products.best_for: A versatile corded multi-tool with fast attachment changes
products.key_spec: 220W, 20,000rpm top speed, 1.4° oscillation angle, magnetic Starlock tool holder, 1.1kg
products.summary: Expert Reviews found an excellent, versatile corded model that comes with a sanding head and paper inserts plus straight and circular blades, along with a depth gauge and plastic case; the side handle for heavier jobs is sold separately. The magnetic tool holder uses a universal screw system, and Bosch claims you can switch attachments in three seconds, though its proprietary Starlock fitting means generic universal blades won't fit. The 220W motor and four-position depth gauge make short work of most cutting jobs.
pros: Depth gauge helps control cuts precisely
Comes with sanding, straight and circular blade attachments
cons: Proprietary Starlock fitting limits blade compatibility

products.name: Tools 430787 DIY Multi Tool
products.best_for: Occasional DIY jobs on a tight budget
products.key_spec: 300W, 23,000rpm top speed, 3° oscillation angle, six-stage speed selector, hex key blade change, 1.45kg
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this a bargain: a mains-powered 300W motor with a maximum 23,000rpm oscillation rate should slice through most jobs, with a six-stage selector to build up power for cutting then rein it back if debris starts flying. It comes with a flat blade, curved blade, sanding shoe, paper inserts and the hex key needed to swap them, though there's no attachable side handle and vibration can be a problem. Replacement blade packs cost almost as much as the tool itself.
cons: Requires a hex key to change blades
No side handle, vibration can be an issue
Replacement blades are pricey relative to the tool

products.name: 20VMAX Cordless Oscillating Multi-Tool Kit
products.best_for: Buyers who want a complete cordless kit with nothing missing
products.key_spec: 20V, 15,000rpm top speed, 1-hour fast charger and battery included, quick-release blade lever, LED work light, 2.78kg
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a rare cordless multi-tool sold as a complete set: inside the case is the tool, a 20V battery, a fast charger that fills it within an hour, three saw blades, a scraper and a sanding shoe with ten inserts, so you can unpack it and start work straight away. Blades change via a quick-release lever that also houses an LED work light. The only thing missing is a side handle to help grip the tool.
pros: Complete kit with battery, charger and blades included
Quick-release blade changing with built-in LED light
cons: No side handle for extra grip
Lower top speed than the corded models here

products.name: DWE315KT 300W Oscillating Multi-Tool
products.best_for: Regular or professional use where you don't want to miss any attachment
products.key_spec: 300W, 22,000rpm top speed, 1.6° oscillation angle, 37-piece accessory set, work light, dust-extraction adapter, 2.0kg
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a tool aimed squarely at professionals, larger than most and lacking the side handle that makes these tools easier to manage, but with a remarkable 37-piece accessory set: a nail-cutting wood blade, grout removal blade, sanding head with 25 inserts, semi-circular and straight wood blades, a scraper, depth gauge, dust-extraction adapter and two hex keys. A powerful work light illuminates the cutting surface, and a universal adapter lets you attach extra blades beyond the included set.
pros: Powerful work light and dust-extraction adapter
Universal adapter for extra blade compatibility
cons: Pricier and larger than most multi-tools

guide.a: A corded model like the Bosch, Silverline or DeWalt works all day without recharging and suits occasional use near a power socket. A cordless model like the Teeno gives freedom of movement, useful if you're already invested in a battery system or working somewhere without easy power access.

A wider oscillation angle, like the Silverline's 3°, cuts more quickly, while a narrower angle, like the Bosch's 1.4°, generally gives a higher-quality finish. Choose based on whether speed or precision matters more for your typical jobs.

Common attachments include cutting blades, grinding discs, sanding shoes and grout-removal blades. The DeWalt comes with a huge 37-piece set covering most jobs out of the box, while the Silverline and Teeno include a smaller core set that covers the basics.

guide.q: Should I check the blade fitting system?
guide.a: Some brands, like Bosch's Starlock system, use proprietary fittings that limit you to that brand's own blades, while others use a more universal fitting or adapter, as on the DeWalt. Check this before buying extra blades to avoid compatibility surprises.
